components-fileuploader-fileuploaderdropcontainer · ./src/components/file-uploader/file-uploader-drop-container.stories.gts
A drop target for files, with a hidden file picker as the click/keyboard fallback. It calls `@onAddFiles` with the added files (each marked `invalidFileType` when it doesn’t match `@accept` or exceeds `@maxFileSize`), but doesn’t list them: render a `FileUploaderItem` per file next to it, so each file’s status can progress on its own. See the drag-and-drop example applications on the `FileUploader` page.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@accept` | `string[]` |  | Specify the types of files that this input should be able to receive |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether file input is disabled |
| `@id` | `string` |  | Provide a unique id for the underlying `<input>` node |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  | Provide the label text to be read by screen readers when interacting with this control |
| `@maxFileSize` | `number` |  | Maximum file size allowed in bytes. Files larger than this are marked invalid |
| `@multiple` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the component should accept multiple files to upload |
| `@name` | `string` |  | Provide a name for the underlying `<input>` node |
| `@onAddFiles` | `(event: Event, data: { addedFiles: FileUploaderAddedFile[]; }) => void` |  | Called after files are added, either by drop or by the file picker |
| `@pattern` | `string` |  | Provide a custom regex pattern used to extract a file's extension |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLButtonElement`.
Imports 
import { FileUploaderDropContainer } from 'carbon-components-ember/components';
Default story ok 
<FileUploaderDropContainer
  @disabled={{false}}
  @labelText="Drag and drop files here or click to upload"
  @multiple={{true}}
  @name=""
/>

FileUploaderItem

components-fileuploader-fileuploaderitem · ./src/components/file-uploader/file-uploader-item.stories.gts
One selected file in a `FileUploader`: its name plus a status icon that follows `@status` (`uploading`, `complete`, or `edit`, which shows a delete button that calls `@onDelete` with the item’s `@uuid`). `@invalid` shows `@errorSubject`/`@errorBody` below it. Render one per file next to a `FileUploaderDropContainer` to build a drag-and-drop upload flow.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the file uploader item is disabled |
| `@errorBody` | `string` |  | Error message body for an invalid file upload |
| `@errorSubject` | `string` |  | Error message subject for an invalid file upload |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Description of the status icon (read by assistive technology) |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the currently uploaded file is invalid |
| `@name` | `string` |  | Name of the uploaded file |
| `@onDelete` | `(event: Event, data: { uuid: string; }) => void` |  | Called after the item is removed, with the item's `uuid` |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  | Specify the size of the item, from a list of available sizes |
| `@status` | `"complete" \| "edit" \| "uploading"` |  | Status of the file upload |
| `@uuid` | `string` |  | Unique identifier for the file, generated when omitted |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLSpanElement`.

FlexGrid

elements-flexgrid · ./src/components/grid/flex-grid.stories.gts
The Flexbox flavour of the 2x Grid: a grid renders one or more `Row`s, and each `Row` renders one or more `Column`s. `FlexGrid` is an always-flexbox alias of `Grid` (whose default `@mode` is `flexbox` anyway), for parity with Carbon React. See *Elements/Grid* for the column span shorthand and the CSS Grid.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  |  |
| `@align` | `GridAlign` |  | Taken for parity with Carbon React; alignment only applies to the CSS Grid, so it has no effect here. |
| `@condensed` | `boolean` |  | Collapse the gutter to 1px. Useful for fluid layouts. Rows have 1px of margin between them to match gutter. |
| `@fullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Remove the default max width that the grid has set |
| `@narrow` | `boolean` |  | Container hangs 16px into the gutter. Useful for typographic alignment with and without containers. |
| `@withRowGap` | `boolean` |  | Add a row gap to the grid that matches the current gutter size. |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `grid` (`GridBlock`)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

FluidTextInput

components-fluid-components-fluidtextinput · ./src/components/fluid-text-input.stories.gts
FluidTextInput is a text input variant with fluid styling - a full-width bottom divider and inline validation message, intended for use in fluid forms. Pass `@defaultValue` for an uncontrolled field, or `@value` with `@onChange` to control it. `@isPassword` masks the value and adds a visibility toggle. The `labelText` block replaces `@labelText` when the label needs markup.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@className` | `string` |  | Carbon React's `className`: classes for the wrapper, or for the `<input>` with `@isPassword`, as in React. `class` and the other attributes go on the `<input>`. |
| `@id` | `string` |  |  |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@value` | `string` |  |  |
| `@defaultValue` | `string` |  |  |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@warn` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@warnText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@enableCounter` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@maxCount` | `number` |  |  |
| `@isPassword` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@showPasswordLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `@hidePasswordLabel` | `string` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(event: Event & { target: HTMLInputElement; }) => void` |  | Called with the `input` event on each change, as Carbon React's `onChange`; the value is `event.target.value`. |
| `@onTogglePasswordVisibility` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- `<:labelText>`

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLInputElement`.

`FormGroup` renders a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, used to group related form controls together under a shared heading.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the FormGroup should be disabled |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the FormGroup is invalid |
| `@legendId` | `string` |  | Provide id for the fieldset legend which corresponds to the fieldset `aria-labelledby` |
| `@legendText` (required) | `string` |  | Provide the text to be rendered inside of the fieldset legend |
| `@message` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the message should be displayed in the FormGroup |
| `@messageText` | `string` |  | Provide the text for the message in the FormGroup |

- default block

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLFieldSetElement`.

Grid

elements-grid · ./src/components/grid.stories.gts
The 2x Grid is a flexible, 16-column grid system that can be used to build custom layouts. Carbon ships two layout engines for it, and `Grid` renders either one: - **Flexbox grid** (the default, `@mode="flexbox"`) — a `Grid` renders one or more `Row`s, and each `Row` renders one or more `Column`s. See *Elements/FlexGrid*. - **CSS Grid** (`@mode="css-grid"`, these stories) — there are no rows; columns are direct children of the `Grid`. This mode additionally supports subgrids, percentage spans, and explicit `start`/`end` placement. `Grid` yields `Grid`, `Column`, `Row` and `ColumnHang` components that are already bound to the surrounding grid's mode, so the mode is only picked once. ### Column span shorthand `Column` accepts a value for each breakpoint (`sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xlg`, `max`): - `true` — the column takes up an equal share of the remaining space - a `number` — the column spans that many columns - an object like `{{hash span=4 offset=2}}` — the column spans `span` columns and is offset by `offset` columns In `css-grid` mode a column additionally accepts a percentage (`'25%'`, `'50%'`, `'75%'`, `'100%'`) and `start`/`end` grid lines.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  |  |
| `@align` | `GridAlign` |  | Specify grid alignment. Default is center. Only applies when `mode` is `css-grid`. |
| `@condensed` | `boolean` |  | Collapse the gutter to 1px. Useful for fluid layouts. Rows have 1px of margin between them to match gutter. |
| `@fullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Remove the default max width that the grid has set |
| `@mode` | `GridMode` | `'flexbox'` | Which layout engine to use. `flexbox` renders `cds--grid`/`cds--row`/ `cds--col-*`, `css-grid` renders `cds--css-grid`/`cds--css-grid-column`. |
| `@narrow` | `boolean` |  | Container hangs 16px into the gutter. Useful for typographic alignment with and without containers. |
| `@subgrid` | `boolean` |  | Render as a subgrid of a surrounding CSS Grid instead of as a new grid. Set automatically for the `Grid` yielded from another `Grid`. |
| `@withRowGap` | `boolean` |  | Add a row gap to the grid that matches the current gutter size. |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `grid` (`GridBlock`)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

Alignment story ok
`@align` positions the grid within its container. It defaults to `center` and only applies in `css-grid` mode. `@align` only has room to move the grid once its container is wider than the grid’s own max width, so the examples are placed in an artificially wide, dashed-outline container that’s wider than the grid itself.

</div>

  </Grid>

elements-grid-gridsettings · ./src/components/grid/grid-settings.stories.gts
`GridSettings` renders no markup of its own. It yields `Grid`, `Column`, `Row` and `ColumnHang` already bound to `@mode`, which is handy when a whole section of an app should share one grid mode. `@subgrid={{true}}` makes the yielded `Grid` render as a subgrid of a surrounding CSS Grid. See *Elements/Grid*.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@mode` | `GridMode` | `'flexbox'` | Specify the gutter mode the yielded grid components should use. |
| `@subgrid` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the yielded `Grid` should render as a subgrid. |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `grid` (`GridBlock`)
Imports 
import { GridSettings } from 'carbon-components-ember/components';

    <g.Column @sm={{4}} @md={{4}} @lg={{4}}><Box>Column 2</Box></g.Column>
    <g.Column @sm={{4}} @md={{4}} @lg={{4}}><Box>Column 3</Box></g.Column>
    <g.Column @sm={{4}} @md={{4}} @lg={{4}}><Box>Column 4</Box></g.Column>
  </g.Grid>
</GridSettings>

Icon

components-icon · ./src/components/icon.stories.gts
`Icon` renders a Carbon SVG icon. Use the generated icon components from `carbon-components-ember/icons` (e.g. `<Bookmark />`), which are 16px unless given `@size`, as in `@carbon/icons-react`, or register an SVG from `@carbon/icons` with `registerIcon(name, svg)` and render it with `<Icon @icon="name" />`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@loading` | `boolean` |  | Indicates if the icon is in loading state |
| `@info` | `boolean` |  | Indicates if the icon is informative |
| `@icon` | `string \| IconType` |  | Use this icon to display |
| `@iconSvg` | `TrustedHTML` |  | Use this icon svg to display, marked as trusted with `trustHTML()` |
| `@size` | `string \| number` |  | Size of the icon, 16 by default, as in `@carbon/icons-react`. A size the icon has no artwork for scales its 32px drawing; `"glyph"` draws its glyph, where it has one. |
| `@svgClass` | `string` |  | Classes for the `<svg>`, as `@carbon/icons-react`'s `className`. |
| `@fill` | `string` |  |  |
| `@title` | `string` |  | Text for an SVG `<title>` element inside the icon, making it accessible to screen readers. Matches `@carbon/icons-react`'s `children` pattern (callers pass `<title>{description}</title>` as children). An empty string renders an empty `<title></title>`, matching React's behaviour when a description prop is present but empty. |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  | Labels the icon for assistive technology, making it an image (`role="img"`) rather than decorative. |

IconIndicator

preview-statusindicators-preview-iconindicator · ./src/components/icon-indicator.stories.gts
Icon indicators pair a status icon with a label to communicate the state of an item. They support the kinds `failed`, `caution-major`, `caution-minor`, `undefined`, `succeeded`, `normal`, `in-progress`, `incomplete`, `not-started`, `pending`, `unknown`, and `informative`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "top-start" \| "top-end" \| "bottom-start" \| "bottom-end" \| "left-end" \| "left-start" \| "right-end" \| "right-start"` |  | Specify how the tooltip should align with the icon in compact mode |
| `@autoAlign` | `boolean` |  | Will auto-align the tooltip in compact mode so it stays within the viewport, moving it to another side when it would otherwise overflow |
| `@compact` | `boolean` |  | When true, displays only the icon with the label in a tooltip |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Description for the icon announced to screen readers in compact mode. Defaults to `label` when not provided. |
| `@kind` (required) | `"undefined" \| "failed" \| "caution-major" \| "caution-minor" \| "succeeded" \| "normal" \| "in-progress" \| "incomplete" \| "not-started" \| "pending" \| "unknown" \| "informative"` |  | Specify the kind of icon to be used |
| `@label` (required) | `string` |  | Label next to the icon |
| `@size` | `16 \| 20` |  | Specify the size of the Icon Indicator. Defaults to 16. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

      @autoAlign={{false}}
      @compact={{false}}
      @iconDescription="Icon"
      @size={{16}}
    />
  {{/each}}
</div>

InlineLoading

components-inlineloading · ./src/components/inline-loading.stories.gts
Shows that something is in progress, finished or failed, in place of the control that started it. `@status` is `inactive`, `active` (the default), `finished` or `error`; `@description` is the text next to the icon, and `@iconDescription` labels the icon. `@onSuccess` runs `@successDelay` milliseconds (1500 by default) after the status becomes `finished`, which is the moment to swap the original control back in.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@status` | `InlineLoadingStatus` |  | The loading status. Defaults to `"active"`. |
| `@description` | `string` |  | Text shown next to the icon. |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Labels the icon. Defaults to "loading", or to the status when it's finished or an error. |
| `@onSuccess` | `() => void` |  | Called `@successDelay` milliseconds after `@status` becomes `"finished"`. |
| `@successDelay` | `number` |  | How long to wait before calling `@onSuccess`, in milliseconds. Defaults to 1500. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import { InlineLoading } from 'carbon-components-ember/components';
Ux Example story ok 
<div class="cds--btn-set inline-loading-story__btn-set">
  <Button
    @kind="secondary"
    @disabled={{or submission.submit.isRunning submission.success}}
  >Cancel</Button>
  {{#if (or submission.submit.isRunning submission.success)}}
    <InlineLoading
      class="inline-loading-story__status"
      @status={{if submission.success "finished" "active"}}
      @description={{if submission.success "Submitted!" "Submitting..."}}
      @onSuccess={{submission.reset}}
    />
  {{else}}
    <Button {{on "click" submission.submit.perform}}>Submit</Button>
  {{/if}}
</div>
Default story ok 
<InlineLoading @description="Loading" @iconDescription="Loading data..." @status="active" />
Without ember-concurrency story ok 
{{#if (or state.submitting state.success)}}
  <InlineLoading
    @status={{if state.success "finished" "active"}}
    @description={{if state.success "Submitted!" "Submitting..."}}
    @onSuccess={{reset}}
  />
{{else}}
  <Button {{on "click" submit}}>Submit</Button>
{{/if}}

InlineNotification

components-notifications-inline · ./src/components/notification/inline.stories.gts
Inline notifications show up in task flows, usually at the top of the primary content area or next to the item they relate to, to tell users the status of an action. They can't contain interactive elements or rich text, don't take focus, and are announced by screen readers when rendered (`role="status"`; set `role="alert"` or `role="log"` for another announcement). They don't close on their own: they stay until the user closes them or resolves the issue, and the close button is optional (`@hideCloseButton`). For an action, use an `ActionableNotification` with `@inline`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  | Provide a description for the "close" icon button that can be read by screen readers. Carbon React's `aria-label`; an `aria-label` attribute would label the notification instead. |
| `@hideCloseButton` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the close button should be hidden. |
| `@kind` | `NotificationKind` |  | Specify what state the notification represents. Defaults to `'error'`. |
| `@lowContrast` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether you are using the low contrast variant of the InlineNotification. |
| `@onClose` | `(event: MouseEvent) => boolean \| void` |  | Provide a function that is called when the close button closes the notification. Return `false` to keep it open. |
| `@onCloseButtonClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  | Provide a function that is called when the close button is clicked. |
| `@statusIconDescription` | `string` |  | Provide a description for the "status" icon that can be read by screen readers. Defaults to `'<kind> icon'`. |
| `@subtitle` | `string` |  | Specify the subtitle. |
| `@title` | `string` |  | Specify the title. |

## Blocks

- default block: More content, after the subtitle. Don't put interactive elements here; use an `ActionableNotification` for those.

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.
Imports 
import { InlineNotification } from 'carbon-components-ember/components';
Default story ok 
<InlineNotification
  @ariaLabel="closes notification"
  @hideCloseButton={{false}}
  @kind="error"
  @lowContrast={{false}}
  @onClose={{@onClose}}
  @onCloseButtonClick={{@onCloseButtonClick}}
  @statusIconDescription="notification"
  @subtitle="Subtitle text goes here"
  @title="Notification title"
/>

API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@showUnreadIndicator` | `boolean` |  | Shows the unread indicator dot when `true` and `@unreadMessageCount` is 0. |
| `@unreadMessageCount` | `number` |  | Number of unread messages. Displays a count badge when greater than 0. |
| `@closedLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label shown when the chat window is closed (launcher is in its "open chat" state). |
| `@openLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the launcher's "close chat" state. Declared for parity with upstream's `cds-aichat-launcher` (it takes an `open-label` attribute), but upstream's own computed aria-label never actually reads it — only `closedLabel`/`unreadLabel` feed it, in every released version through 1.9.0. This port matches that behaviour rather than "fixing" it, since the launcher itself has no open/closed state to key off (see the class doc below). |
| `@aiEnabled` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, renders the AI launch icon. When `false`, renders the standard chat launch icon. |
| `@launcherAvatarUrl` | `string` |  | Optional URL for a custom avatar image. When provided, the avatar replaces the default icon. |
| `@unreadLabel` | `string` |  | Pre-formatted screen-reader label suffix for the unread message count (e.g. "3 unread messages"). Appended to the button's aria-label when set. |
| `@tooltipPosition` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` |  | Tooltip position when hovering over the launcher. Defaults to `'top'`. |
| `@onToggle` | `() => void` |  | Called when the user clicks the launcher button. |

Layer

components-layer · ./src/components/layer.stories.gts
The `Layer` component renders content on a specific Carbon layer. Each layer has a set of token values associated with it, which other components (like `Tile`) key off of to determine their own background. You can use these tokens directly, or use contextual tokens from Carbon's styles package like `$layer` or `$field`. `Layer`s can be nested up to three levels deep; past that, the level stays clamped at the third level. Ember has no equivalent of React's ambient `LayerContext`, so a bare `<Layer>` always renders as the first level of nesting; to nest `Layer`s more than one level deep, use the component yielded to the block, which is pre-bound to the correct next level: ```hbs <Layer as |L|> ... <L>...</L> </Layer> ```
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | Specify the element type to render, defaults to `div` |
| `@level` | `LayerLevel` |  | Specify the layer level and override any existing level based on hierarchy. Defaults to `1`, which matches the page's implicit base layer (see `<Theme>`, which applies `cds--layer-one` at the root). |
| `@withBackground` | `boolean` |  | Applies a background color set to the layer's `$layer-background` token |

## Blocks

- default block: Yields a `Layer` pre-bound to the correct next nesting level. Ember has no equivalent of React's ambient `LayerContext`, so a bare `<Layer>` always renders as if it were the first level of nesting (matching the common case); use the yielded component to nest `Layer`s more than one level deep so each one's level increments correctly.
  - yields `Layer` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.
Imports 
import { Layer } from 'carbon-components-ember/components';

  </L>
</Layer>

    <div class="layer-story__box-no-background">Workspace settings</div>
  </L>
</Layer>

  <div class="layer-story__box">Workspace settings</div>
</Layer>

Layout

preview-preview-layout · ./src/components/layout.stories.gts
The `Layout` component provides a way to set layout contexts for specific parts of an application. It uses Carbon's experimental `layout` Sass module to control layout-related settings like size and density for all components rendered within it that support these options. All children components that support it will react to the `@size` and `@density` you pass to `Layout`. Note that not all components support the entire spectrum of options available; in these cases a component will typically cap out at the maximum or minimum size it supports. If a component is outside of a layout context, or `@size` / `@density` isn't set, it falls back to its default rendering.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | The element type to render Layout as. |
| `@density` | `LayoutDensity` |  | Specify the desired density of components within this layout. |
| `@size` | `LayoutSize` |  | Specify the desired size of components within this layout. |

## Blocks

- default block

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.
Imports 
import { Layout } from 'carbon-components-ember/components';

</Stack>

preview-preview-layout-layoutconstraint · ./src/components/layout-constraint.stories.gts
Applies layout constraints to its children that might differ from their own preference or from the surrounding `Layout` context. The constraints for each group (`@size` and `@density`) are passed as an object with any of the keys `min`, `default` and `max`, e.g. `{{hash default="sm" min="sm" max="lg"}}`.

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | The element type to render LayoutConstraint as. |
| `@density` | `LayoutConstraintValue` |  | Specify the desired layout density constraints of this element's children. |
| `@size` | `LayoutConstraintValue` |  | Specify the desired layout size constraints of this element's children. |

## Blocks

- default block

LayoutDirection

components-layoutdirection · ./src/components/layout-direction.stories.gts
The `LayoutDirection` component sets the reading direction (`ltr` or `rtl`) for a part of the page. It renders a wrapper element with a `dir` attribute, which the browser natively cascades to descendant elements. `LayoutDirection` components can be nested to override the direction for a specific section of content. The block receives `dir` and `isRTL` so nested content can react to the active direction, mirroring React's `useLayoutDirection` hook.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  |  |
| `@dir` (required) | `LayoutDirectionType` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields a hash:
    - `dir`: `LayoutDirectionType`
    - `isRTL`: `boolean`

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

LineChart

charts-linechart · ./src/components/charts/line-chart.stories.gts
A line chart, rendered by `@carbon/charts`: one line per `TabularData` group. It yields `Axis` (one each for `left` and `bottom`, both required), `TabularData` (from `@values` plus `@keys` or `@dates`, or from `@data`), `ColorScale` (a color per group) and `ColorPairing` (a Carbon color pairing). Load `@carbon/charts/styles.css` alongside the Carbon styles.

| `@resizable` | `boolean` |  | Whether the chart resizes with its container. Defaults to `true`. |
| `@legendClickable` | `boolean` |  | Whether clicking a legend item shows or hides its data. Defaults to `true`. |

Link

components-link · ./src/components/link.stories.gts
Links are used as navigational elements. They may be used on their own, within a sentence or paragraph, or directly following the content they are relevant to. Link to a URL with `@href`, or to one of the app's routes with `@route` (plus `@models` and `@query`), which renders Ember's `LinkTo`: it navigates without reloading the page and has the `active` class while its route is current.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@route` | `string` |  | Links to this route through the Ember router, in place of `@href`, as Ember's `LinkTo`: the link navigates without reloading the page. |
| `@models` | `unknown[]` |  | The models for `@route`'s dynamic segments, in order. |
| `@query` | `Record<string, unknown>` |  | Query params for `@route`. |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | Provide a custom element or component to render the top-level node for the component. Defaults to `a`. It overrides `@route`. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the control should be disabled, or not. |
| `@href` | `string` |  | Provide the `href` attribute for the `<a>` node. |
| `@inline` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether you want the inline version of this control. |
| `@renderIcon` | `ComponentLike<{ Args: { size?: string \| number \| undefined; svgClass?: string \| undefined; }; }>` |  | A component used to render an icon, drawn at 16px (as Carbon React). |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  | Specify the size of the Link. Currently supports either `sm`, `md` (default) or `lg` as an option. |
| `@target` | `string` |  | Specify the target attribute for the `<a>` node. |
| `@visited` | `boolean` |  | When enabled, applies Carbon's visited-link styles to browser-controlled `:visited` link state. |
| `@onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  | Called when the link is clicked, unless it is disabled. |

## Blocks

- default block

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLElement`.

Markdown

ai-chat-markdown · ./src/components/ai-chat/markdown.stories.gts
`Markdown` parses `@markdown` with `markdown-it` (CommonMark, plus tables, strikethrough, autolinking, GFM task lists, and `==highlight==` extended syntax) and renders it as sanitized, Carbon-styled HTML. Unlike upstream's `cds-aichat-markdown`, rendered HTML is **always** run through DOMPurify before being injected, regardless of `@sanitizeHTML` — see the component's class doc for the full reasoning. Set `@removeHTML={{true}}` to strip raw HTML from the source entirely instead of just sanitizing it.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@markdown` | `string` |  | Direct markdown source input. Always-controlled, always-authoritative. |
| `@sanitizeHTML` | `boolean` |  | Accepted for API parity with upstream's `sanitize-html` attribute, but not wired to anything: this port always sanitizes rendered HTML via DOMPurify, regardless of this flag. See `-markdown-render.ts`'s `renderMarkdown` doc for why. |
| `@removeHTML` | `boolean` |  | Strip all raw HTML from the parsed markdown. Defaults to `false`. |
| `@streaming` | `boolean` |  | Throttles re-render to at most once per 100ms (leading + trailing), matching upstream's own default streaming throttle - reduces layout thrash while a caller is appending markdown token-by-token. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

Menu

components-menu · ./src/components/menu.stories.gts
Menu is a low-level building block for rendering a floating list of actions; `OverflowMenu` and context menus are built on top of it. It's a controlled component: pass `@open` and toggle it from `@onClose`/your own trigger. Compose it out of `MenuItem`, `MenuItemDivider`, `MenuItemGroup`, `MenuItemRadioGroup`, and `MenuItemSelectable`. By default the Menu renders into `document.body`; `@target` renders it into another element. `@x`/`@y` position it; passing both edges of a trigger (`[x1, x2]`/`[y1, y2]`) lets it flip to the other side when it doesn't fit. Clicking a leaf item, pressing <kbd>Escape</kbd>, or moving focus outside the menu all call `@onClose`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@label` (required) | `string` |  | A required label describing the Menu (used as `aria-label`). |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the Menu is open or not. |
| `@backgroundToken` | `"layer" \| "background"` |  | Specify the background token to use. Default is 'layer'. |
| `@border` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a border should be rendered on the menu. |
| `@menuAlignment` | `string` |  | Specify how the menu should align with the button element. Only `top`/`top-start`/`top-end` affect rendering (adds a top box-shadow). |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xs"` |  | Specify the size of the Menu. Only respected on the top-level Menu; submenus always inherit the size of their root Menu. |
| `@target` | `Element` |  | Specify a DOM node where the Menu should be rendered in. Defaults to `document.body`. Pass a node inside your own root when the Menu is rendered in a shadow root, otherwise it escapes into the light DOM where your styles don't reach it. Submenus aren't portaled - they inherit this as their positioning origin instead. |
| `@x` | `number \| [number, number]` |  | Specify the x position of the Menu. Either pass a single number or an array with two numbers describing your activator's boundaries ([x1, x2]). |
| `@y` | `number \| [number, number]` |  | Specify the y position of the Menu. Either pass a single number or an array with two numbers describing your activator's boundaries ([y1, y2]). |
| `@onOpen` | `() => void` |  | Provide an optional function to be called when the Menu is opened. |
| `@onClose` | `() => void` |  | Provide an optional function to be called when the Menu should be closed, including if the Menu is blurred, the user presses escape, or the Menu is a submenu and the user presses ArrowLeft. |
| `@isRoot` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@anchor` | `HTMLElement` |  |  |

- default block

Modal

components-modal · ./src/components/modal.stories.gts
Modals focus the user's attention exclusively on one task or piece of information. `Modal` is a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`: it shows above the rest of the page, which is inert while it's open, and returns focus to where it was when it closes. It needs no element in the application template. Anything rendered outside it, such as a toast or a menu rendered elsewhere in the page, stays under it and can't be used while it's open. `@open` shows it. Closing is up to you: the close button, Escape, the secondary button and, for a passive modal, a click outside call `@onRequestClose`, and the primary button calls `@onRequestSubmit`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@alert` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the Modal is displaying an alert, error or warning Should go hand in hand with the danger prop. |
| `@closeButtonLabel` | `string` |  | Specify label for the close button of the modal; defaults to close |
| `@danger` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the Modal is for dangerous actions |
| `@dangerDescription` | `string` |  | Specify the message read by screen readers for the danger primary button. Defaults to an empty string; provide localized text to opt in. |
| `@hasScrollingContent` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the modal contains scrolling content |
| `@id` | `string` |  | Specify the DOM element ID of the top-level node. |
| `@isFullWidth` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether or not the Modal content should have any inner padding. |
| `@loadingDescription` | `string` |  | Specify the description for the loading text |
| `@loadingIconDescription` | `string` |  | Specify the description for the loading text |
| `@loadingStatus` | `InlineLoadingStatus` |  | Specify loading status |
| `@modalAriaLabel` | `string` |  | Specify a label to be read by screen readers on the modal root node |
| `@modalHeading` | `string` |  | Specify the content of the modal header title. |
| `@modalLabel` | `string` |  | Specify the content of the modal header label. |
| `@onLoadingSuccess` | `() => void` |  | Specify an optional handler to be invoked when loading is successful |
| `@onRequestClose` | `(event: Event) => void` |  | Specify a handler for closing modal. The handler should take care of closing modal, e.g. changing `@open`. |
| `@onRequestSubmit` | `(event: Event) => void` |  | Specify a handler for "submitting" modal. The handler should take care of closing modal, e.g. changing `@open`, if necessary. |
| `@onSecondarySubmit` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  | Specify a handler for the secondary button. Useful if separate handler from `onRequestClose` is desirable |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the Modal is currently open |
| `@passiveModal` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the modal should be button-less |
| `@preventCloseOnClickOutside` | `boolean` |  | Prevent closing on click outside of modal. A passive modal closes on one unless this is set; any other closes only when it's `false`. |
| `@primaryButtonDisabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the Button should be disabled, or not |
| `@primaryButtonText` | `string` |  | Specify the text for the primary button |
| `@secondaryButtonText` | `string` |  | Specify the text for the secondary button |
| `@secondaryButtons` | `ModalSecondaryButton[]` |  | Specify an array of config objects for secondary buttons, at most two |
| `@selectorPrimaryFocus` | `string` |  | Specify a CSS selector that matches the DOM element that should be focused when the Modal opens |
| `@shouldSubmitOnEnter` | `boolean` |  | Specify if Enter key should be used as "submit" action |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xs"` |  | Specify the size variant. |

## Blocks

- default block: The modal's content.
- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown in the header. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDialogElement`.

MultiSelect

components-multiselect · ./src/components/multi-select.stories.gts
`MultiSelect` is a field that opens a listbox of checkable items, for choosing any number of them. Like Carbon React's, it's built on the ListBox parts and follows downshift's keyboard model: focus stays on the field while the arrow keys move the highlight, Space or Enter checks the highlighted item, and the menu stays open until Escape, Tab or a click elsewhere. A tag in the field counts the items chosen and clears them; so do Delete and Escape on the closed field. Items can be any value: `@itemToString` turns one into its text (by default, a string or number item itself, or an object's string `label`). An item with `disabled: true` can't be chosen, and one with `isSelectAll: true` checks or clears every other item. The menu lists items by text, with the selection first once it reopens; `@selectionFeedback`, `@sortItems` and `@compareItems` change that.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@id` | `string` |  | The id of the field. The label, button, menu and items derive theirs from it. Auto-generated when omitted. |
| `@items` (required) | `T[]` |  | The items to choose from. They can be any value: `@itemToString` turns one into its text. An item with `disabled: true` can't be chosen, and one with `isSelectAll: true` selects or clears every other item. Object items with an `undefined` value aren't listed, as in Carbon React. |
| `@itemToString` | `(item: T) => string` |  | Turns an item into the text shown for it. Defaults to a string or number item itself, or an object's string `label`. |
| `@label` (required) | `string` |  | The text in the field, whatever is selected. |
| `@titleText` | `string` |  | The field's label, above it. |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Visually hide `@titleText`, keeping it for assistive technology. |
| `@helperText` | `string` |  | Help shown below the field, unless it's invalid or warning. |
| `@selectedItems` | `T[]` |  | The selected items, for full control of the selection: pair it with `@onChange`. Wins over internal state whenever it's defined. |
| `@initialSelectedItems` | `T[]` |  | The items selected at first, for the uncontrolled case. Later changes are ignored. |
| `@onChange` | `(data: MultiSelectChange<T>) => void` |  | Called with the new selection whenever it changes. |
| `@onMenuChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with `true` when the menu opens and `false` when it closes. |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the menu is open. It seeds the menu's state, and opens or closes the menu whenever it changes. |
| `@selectionFeedback` | `"top" \| "fixed" \| "top-after-reopen"` |  | Where chosen items go in the list: `top` moves them to the top at once, `top-after-reopen` (the default) the next time the menu opens, and `fixed` leaves them in place. |
| `@sortItems` | `(items: readonly T[], options: SortItemsOptions<T>) => T[]` |  | Orders the items. The default puts a select-all option first, then the selected items (as `@selectionFeedback` says), then the rest by `@compareItems`. To only change how items compare, pass that instead. |
| `@compareItems` | `CompareItems` |  | Compares two items' texts for the default order. Defaults to `localeCompare` in `@locale`, with numbers compared by value. |
| `@locale` | `string` |  | The locale the default `@compareItems` sorts in. Defaults to `en`. |
| `@clearSelectionDescription` | `string` |  | Read to assistive technology before the number selected. Defaults to "Total items selected: ". |
| `@clearSelectionText` | `string` |  | Read to assistive technology after the items selected. Defaults to "To clear selection, press Delete or Backspace". |
| `@clearAnnouncement` | `string` |  | Announced when Delete clears the selection. Defaults to "all items have been cleared". |
| `@useTitleInItem` | `boolean` |  | Show each item's text as its checkbox's tooltip. |
| `@autoAlign` | `boolean` |  | **Experimental:** position the menu with Floating UI, so it opens above the field when there's no room below, and hides when the field scrolls out of view. |
| `@direction` | `"top" \| "bottom"` |  | The side of the field the menu opens on. Defaults to `bottom`. |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xs"` |  | The field's height. Without it, the field follows an enclosing Layout's size. |
| `@type` | `"default" \| "inline"` |  | `inline` lays the field out next to its label. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the control should be disabled, or not. |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Whether the selection can be read and focused, but not changed. |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the current selection is invalid. |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the selection is invalid. |
| `@warn` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the control is currently in warning state. |
| `@warnText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the control is in warning state. |

## Blocks

- default block: Renders each item's text in the menu. Defaults to `@itemToString`.
  - yields `item` (`T`)
- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown in the field. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

NumberInput

components-numberinput · ./src/components/number-input.stories.gts
NumberInput allows the user to enter a number, and to increment/decrement the value using stepper buttons. Pass `@defaultValue` for an uncontrolled input, or `@value` with `@onChange` to control it; `@onChange` receives the event and `{ value, direction }`, as in Carbon React.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@className` | `string` |  | Classes for the wrapper, as Carbon React's `className`. `class` and the other attributes go on the `<input>`. |
| `@id` | `string` |  |  |
| `@label` | `string` |  |  |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@value` | `number \| ""` |  |  |
| `@defaultValue` | `number \| ""` |  |  |
| `@min` | `number` |  |  |
| `@max` | `number` |  |  |
| `@step` | `number` |  |  |
| `@stepStartValue` | `number` |  |  |
| `@allowEmpty` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@warn` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@warnText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@helperText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@hideSteppers` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` |  |  |
| `@light` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(event: Event, state: { value: number \| ""; direction: "up" \| "down"; }) => void` |  | Called on each change, as Carbon React's `onChange`: with the `input` event when typing, or the stepper's `click` event, and the new value and the direction it moved in. |
| `@onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  |  |
| `@onBlur` | `(event: FocusEvent) => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown in the field. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLInputElement`.

OrderedList

components-orderedlist · ./src/components/ordered-list.stories.gts
Ordered lists are groupings of related content where the order of the items within the group is meaningful. Each item is a `ListItem`: a single `<li>` with the styles it needs to work as a child of `OrderedList` or `UnorderedList`. It has no arguments of its own; any attributes passed to it (`id`, `class`, ...) are applied to the underlying `<li>`. A `ListItem` can contain a nested list to build multi-level lists.
API description

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

OverflowMenu

components-overflowmenu · ./src/components/overflow-menu.stories.gts
A button that opens a menu of actions for the thing it sits next to. It yields `OverflowMenuItem` bound to the menu: an item closes the menu once its `{{on "click"}}` has run, and the arrow keys move between enabled items. The menu renders in place, in the top layer, so containers like DataTable cells don't clip it and it stays usable inside a Modal. `@iconDescription` names the trigger and is its tooltip; `@ariaLabel` names the menu.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "top-left" \| "top-start" \| "top-right" \| "top-end" \| "bottom-left" \| "bottom-start" \| "bottom-right" \| "bottom-end" \| "left-bottom" \| "left-end" \| "left-top" \| "left-start" \| "right-bottom" \| "right-end" \| "right-top" \| "right-start"` |  | How the trigger's tooltip is aligned. Defaults to `top`. |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  | Names the menu for assistive technology, as Carbon React's `aria-label`, which labels the menu rather than the trigger. |
| `@autoAlign` | `boolean` |  | Aligns the trigger's tooltip to stay in view. |
| `@closeOnActivation` | `boolean` |  | Hides the trigger's tooltip when the trigger is pressed. Defaults to `true`. |
| `@defaultOpen` | `boolean` |  | Shows the trigger's tooltip on the first render. |
| `@direction` | `OverflowMenuDirection` |  | The side of the trigger the menu opens on, when there's room for it there; otherwise it opens on the other side. Defaults to `bottom`. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables the trigger. |
| `@dropShadow` | `boolean` |  | Gives the trigger's tooltip a drop shadow. |
| `@enterDelayMs` | `number` |  | Milliseconds before the trigger's tooltip shows. Defaults to 100. |
| `@flipped` | `boolean` |  | Lines the menu's end edge up with the trigger's, instead of its start edge. |
| `@highContrast` | `boolean` |  | Gives the trigger's tooltip high contrast. Defaults to `true`. |
| `@iconClass` | `string` |  | Classes for the trigger's icon. |
| `@iconDescription` | `string` |  | Names the trigger, and is its tooltip. Defaults to "Options". |
| `@leaveDelayMs` | `number` |  | Milliseconds before the trigger's tooltip hides. Defaults to 100. |
| `@menuOffset` | `OverflowMenuOffset \| OverflowMenuOffsetFunction` |  | Moves the menu from where it would sit centered on the trigger: `top` away from it, `left` to the right, as Carbon React's. Without it, the menu lines up with the trigger's start edge. |
| `@menuOffsetFlip` | `OverflowMenuOffset \| OverflowMenuOffsetFunction` |  | `@menuOffset` for a `@flipped` menu, lined up with the end edge without it. |
| `@menuOptionsClass` | `string` |  | Classes for the menu. |
| `@onClose` | `() => void` |  | Called when the menu closes. |
| `@onOpen` | `() => void` |  | Called when the menu opens. |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Opens or closes the menu when it changes. |
| `@renderIcon` | `ComponentLike<{ Args: { size?: string \| number \| undefined; svgClass?: string \| undefined; ariaLabel?: string \| undefined; }; }>` |  | The trigger's icon, drawn at 16px. Defaults to OverflowMenuVertical. |
| `@selectorPrimaryFocus` | `string` |  | The element to focus when the menu opens, in it. Defaults to `[data-floating-menu-primary-focus]`, then its first item. |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xs"` |  | The trigger's size. |
| `@wrapperClasses` | `string` |  | Classes for the trigger's tooltip. |

## Blocks

- default block
  - yields `OverflowMenuItem` (component)

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLButtonElement`.

Popover

components-popover · ./src/components/popover.stories.gts
`Popover` is used for triggering a pop-up next to a trigger element, typically a button, in a given direction. It is a controlled component: the consumer owns the `@open` argument and toggles it (usually from the trigger's click handler), while `Popover` calls `@onRequestClose` whenever the user clicks outside of the popover or presses <kbd>Escape</kbd> while focus is inside the popover content. The trigger element and `PopoverContent` are both yielded as plain children of `Popover`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@align` | `PopoverAlignment` |  | Specify how the popover should align with the trigger element. |
| `@alignmentAxisOffset` | `number` |  | **Experimental:** Provide an offset value for alignment axis. Only takes effect when `autoAlign` is enabled. |
| `@as` | `keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap` |  | The element type to render the outermost node as. |
| `@autoAlign` | `boolean` |  | **Experimental:** Positions the content with Floating UI and keeps it within the viewport (or `autoAlignBoundary`, if provided), flipping it to another side when it doesn't fit. The content renders in the top layer, so overflowing ancestors don't clip it. |
| `@autoAlignBoundary` | `any` |  | **Experimental:** Specify a bounding element to be used for autoAlign calculations. The viewport is used by default. |
| `@backgroundToken` | `"layer" \| "background"` |  | Specify the background token to use. Default is 'layer'. |
| `@border` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a border should be rendered on the popover. |
| `@caret` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a caret should be rendered. |
| `@dropShadow` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether a drop shadow should be rendered on the popover. |
| `@highContrast` | `boolean` |  | Render the component using the high-contrast variant. |
| `@isTabTip` | `boolean` |  | Render the component using the tab tip variant. |
| `@onRequestClose` | `() => void` |  | Specify a handler for closing the popover. The handler should take care of closing the popover, e.g. changing the `open` argument. Called when the user clicks outside of the popover or presses Escape while focus is inside the popover content. |
| `@open` (required) | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the component is currently open or closed. |

## Blocks

Portal

components-portal · ./src/components/portal.stories.gts
Helper component for rendering content within a portal. By default, the portal renders into `document.body`. You can customize this behavior with the `@container` argument. Any content yielded to this component will be rendered inside of the container.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@container` | `HTMLElement` |  | Provide a DOM node to render the portal's content into. Defaults to `document.body`. |

PromptLine

ai-chat-prompt-line · ./src/components/ai-chat/prompt-line.stories.gts
`PromptLine` is the editing surface of the chat input stack, typically composed inside a `PromptLineShell`'s `<:editor>` block. It renders a plain `<textarea>` by default and never statically imports `@tiptap/*` — setting `@rich` (or calling `ensureEditor()` off the handle `@onReady` provides) dynamically loads a small Tiptap runtime chunk and upgrades the surface in place, carrying the text, caret, and focus over losslessly. Both modes share the same `@content`/`@onChange`/`@onSendIntent` contract. `@content` is always-controlled: typing only fires `@onChange`, so the host keeps the text and hands it back. Press Enter to send (Shift+Enter inserts a newline instead). `@extensions` accepts plain Tiptap `Extension`s appended to the base Carbon bundle (schema, undo/redo, placeholder, plain-text paste, the Enter/Mod-Enter/Escape keymap) — memoize the array you pass, since a fresh one every render rebuilds the live editor (content, selection, and focus survive; undo history doesn't). ### Mention, command, autocomplete, and starter triggers `buildCarbonExtensions` (and the individual `carbonMention`/`carbonCommand`/`carbonAutocomplete`/`carbonStarterTrigger` factories it wraps, all under `carbon-components-ember/components/ai-chat/-prompt-line/tiptap/`) build Tiptap extensions you pass through `@extensions` like any other — `PromptLine` itself has no dedicated mention/command/autocomplete/starter args, matching upstream's own `<cds-aichat-prompt-line>`. The extensions only dispatch a bubbling `cds-aichat-trigger-change` DOM event with `{ type, query, triggerOffset }`; **the actual popup is `PromptLineAutocomplete`** — pair it with a `PromptLine` via the imperative handle from `@onReady`. A command chip (`/summarize`) is prefixed with its trigger character by default; a mention chip (`Jane Smith`) isn't — either default can be overridden per-config or per-item via `showTriggerInChip`. Mention, command, autocomplete, and starter extensions each react to the *same* document changes and dispatch `cds-aichat-trigger-change` independently — combined on one editor, typing `@` after focusing an empty field can dispatch the starter list's own exit event (`null`) *after* the mention trigger's own opening event. A naive "last event wins" listener can momentarily see a stale `null` and hide its popup even though a trigger is genuinely open. `PromptLineAutocomplete` reconciles this (batches same-tick events by microtask, resolves to the last non-null one) — see the **All triggers** story.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@content` | `string` |  | Current plain-text value. Always-controlled: typing only fires `@onChange`. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `@ariaLabel` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Message'`. |
| `@testId` | `string` |  |  |
| `@autofocus` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Fires with the new value on every input, in either mode. |
| `@onSendIntent` | `() => void` |  | Fires on plain Enter (non-empty field) or Mod-Enter (any field), mirroring upstream's Enter-to-send keymap. Identical in both modes. |
| `@rich` | `boolean` |  | Selects the rich Tiptap editor. Defaults to the textarea. The element lazy-loads Tiptap (a dynamic `import()`, so a chat that never sets this never ships it) and upgrades the textarea to it in place — text, caret, and focus all carry over, so the swap is a same-frame handoff, not a visible reset. The upgrade is **sticky**: once rich, later setting this back to `false` does not downgrade. |
| `@extensions` | `Extension<any, any>[]` |  | Host-supplied Tiptap `Extension`s, appended to the base Carbon bundle (schema, undo/redo, placeholder, plain-text paste, the Enter/Mod-Enter/ Escape keymap) when the rich editor (re)builds. Ignored in textarea mode — setting these alone does not trigger the upgrade. Compared by reference: a fresh array every render rebuilds the live editor (preserving content/selection/focus but resetting undo history), so memoize it rather than passing an inline literal. |
| `@onReady` | `(api: PromptLineApi) => void` |  | Called once, right after mount, with an imperative handle to the surface. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

Default story ok 
<SentMessages @messages={{state.sent}} />
<PromptLineShell
  @rounded={{true}}
  @disabled={{false}}
  @hasError={{false}}
  @expanded={{false}}
>
  <:fieldMessaging>
    {{#if args.hasError}}
      <ErrorMessage
        @title="Something went wrong."
        @description=""
      />
    {{/if}}
  </:fieldMessaging>
  <:editor>
    <PromptLine
      @content={{state.content}}
      @placeholder="Type something..."
      @disabled={{false}}
      @onChange={{state.onChange}}
      @onSendIntent={{state.onSendIntent}}
      @onReady={{state.onReady}}
    />
  </:editor>
  <:messageActions>
    {{#if args.expanded}}
      <InlineActions
        @actions={{ACTIONS}}
        @disabled={{false}}
        @onAction={{@onAction}}
      />
    {{/if}}
  </:messageActions>
  <:sendControl>
    <SendControl
      @label="Send"
      @disabled={{state.sendDisabled}}
      @onSend={{state.send}}
    />
  </:sendControl>
</PromptLineShell>

PromptLineAutocomplete

ai-chat-prompt-line-autocomplete · ./src/components/ai-chat/prompt-line-autocomplete.stories.gts
The suggestion overlay for `PromptLine`'s mention (`@`), command (`/`), autocomplete, and starter-prompt Tiptap extensions (see **AI Chat/Prompt line** for building those). Pair one `PromptLineAutocomplete` with exactly one `PromptLine` via the imperative handle from its `@onReady` — typically composed inside a `PromptLineShell`'s `<:autocompleteContent>` block. Mention and command items always insert into the editor as a chip (a `data-token-type="mention"`/`"command"` node — `disableDirectSend` is forced `true` for these two regardless of config). Autocomplete and starter items default to **sending directly**: clicking one fires `@onItemSend` with its `value ?? label` and never touches the editor at all — the host owns actually sending it (this component carries no chat-domain logic, matching `PromptLineShell`). Set `disableDirectSend: true` on an autocomplete/starters config to switch that trigger's items to the "insert into the editor" path instead, firing `@onItemSelected` (and, for starters specifically, `@onStarterSelected` with the editor's full text) rather than `@onItemSend`. Use the arrow keys, Home/End, Enter and Escape from the editor; disabled items are skipped.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@promptLine` | `PromptLineApi` |  | The `PromptLineApi` handle from the paired `PromptLine`'s `@onReady`. Read only inside event handlers (click, keydown, outside-click) — never during render/modifier setup — so there is no ordering requirement against when the paired `PromptLine`'s `@onReady` actually fires. |
| `@mention` | `TriggerSuggestionConfig` |  | `@`-style mention trigger config. |
| `@command` | `TriggerSuggestionConfig` |  | `/`-style command trigger config. |
| `@autocomplete` | `BaseSuggestionConfig` |  | Live-typeahead autocomplete config (no trigger character). |
| `@starters` | `StartersConfig` |  | Starter prompts shown while the editor is empty and focused. |
| `@isSendDisabled` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, the "send directly" click path (see `BaseSuggestionConfig.disableDirectSend`) becomes a no-op instead of firing `@onItemSend`. |
| `@i18n` | `Partial<AutocompleteI18n>` |  |  |
| `@headerConfig` | `HeaderConfig` |  |  |
| `@onStarterSelected` | `(text: string) => void` |  | Fires after a starter is inserted into the editor (the `disableDirectSend: true` path only) with the editor's full raw text, so the host can trigger send. Skipped when `@isSendDisabled`. |
| `@onItemSelected` | `(item: SuggestionItem) => void` |  | Fires after any item is inserted into the editor (the `disableDirectSend: true` path, all trigger types). |
| `@onItemSend` | `(text: string) => void` |  | Fires when an item is activated on the default "send directly" path (`disableDirectSend` unset/false) with the item's `value ?? label` — this component never touches the editor for this path, the host owns actually sending. Skipped (and the popup stays open) when `@isSendDisabled`. |
| `@target` | `HTMLElement` |  | Ancestor element to listen on for the bubbling `cds-aichat-trigger-change` DOM event, editor keydown forwarding, and outside-click/focusout detection. Defaults to the closest `.cds-aichat-prompt-line-shell` ancestor, or this component's own parent element if there isn't one — override for standalone use (a `PromptLine` not inside a `PromptLineShell`), same spirit as `Menu`'s `@target`/`DatePicker`'s `@appendTo`. |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

PromptLineShell

ai-chat-prompt-line-shell · ./src/components/ai-chat/prompt-line-shell.stories.gts
Layout-only composer chrome for the chat input: `PromptLineShell` defines six named blocks (`<:editor>`, `<:messageActions>`, `<:fileUploads>`, `<:autocompleteContent>`, `<:fieldMessaging>`, `<:sendControl>`) and the spacing/border treatment around them. It carries no chat-domain logic and forwards no editor methods — compose a `PromptLine` (or your own editing surface) into `<:editor>`. See **AI Chat/Prompt line** for compositions with message actions, file uploads and the autocomplete popup.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@rounded` | `boolean` |  | Reflects to a class so consumer CSS can target the rounded variant. |
| `@expanded` | `boolean` |  | Expanded layout: the editor fills its own full-width row, with the message actions and send control on a second row beneath it. The reflow is driven purely by a container class — the rendered DOM is identical in both modes. |
| `@hasError` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hasFileUploads` | `boolean` |  | Whether the `<:fileUploads>` block currently has real uploads to show. Upstream derives this by watching the slotted file-uploads element's own `has-uploads` attribute via a `MutationObserver`; Ember has no equivalent DOM-introspection hook for a block's rendered content, so this port takes it as a plain controlled arg instead — pass it straight through from whatever tracks the upload list. |

## Blocks

- `<:editor>`: A `PromptLine` (or equivalent) the caller owns directly; no fallback is rendered.
- `<:messageActions>`: Action icons beside the text area.
- `<:fileUploads>`: Visual list of files being uploaded.
- `<:autocompleteContent>`: Suggestion overlay above the input.
- `<:fieldMessaging>`: Inline error / status content beneath the autocomplete row.
- `<:sendControl>`: Send / stop-streaming button.

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

RadioButton

components-radiobutton · ./src/components/radio-button.stories.gts
Radio buttons are used when there is a list of two or more options that are mutually exclusive and the user must select exactly one choice. Render them through a `RadioButtonGroup`, which yields a `RadioButton` already wired to the group: the group owns the shared `name`, the selection (`@defaultSelected`, or `@valueSelected` to control it) and reports changes through `@onChange`. A RadioButton can also be used on its own with `@checked`/`@defaultChecked`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@className` | `string` |  | Classes for the wrapper, as Carbon React's `className`. `class` and the other attributes go on the `<input>`. |
| `@id` | `string` |  |  |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@value` | `Value` |  |  |
| `@name` | `string` |  |  |
| `@checked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@defaultChecked` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@labelPosition` | `"right" \| "left"` |  |  |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@required` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@group` | `RadioButtonGroup` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(value: Value \| undefined, name: string \| undefined, event: Event) => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- default block: The label's content. Keep it text: put an AI label or other controls in `<:decorator>`.
- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown after the label. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it; with `@kind="inline"`, also pass `@size="md"`.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLInputElement`.

RadioButtonGroup

components-radiobutton-radiobuttongroup · ./src/components/radio-button/radio-button-group.stories.gts
A `<fieldset>` that groups mutually exclusive `RadioButton`s. It yields a `RadioButton` already wired to the group: the group owns the shared `name`, the selection (`@defaultSelected`, or `@valueSelected` to control it) and reports changes through `@onChange`. The legend is `@legendText`, or the `heading` block for richer content. See `RadioButton` for the buttons themselves.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` |  | Defaults to `'horizontal'`. |
| `@labelPosition` | `"right" \| "left"` |  | Defaults to `'right'`. |
| `@legendText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@name` | `string` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@required` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@valueSelected` | `Value` |  |  |
| `@defaultSelected` | `Value` |  |  |
| `@onChange` | `(value: Value \| undefined, name: string \| undefined, event: Event) => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- `<:heading>`: The legend's content. Keep it text: put an AI label in `<:decorator>`.
- default block
  - yields `RadioButton` (component)
- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown after the legend. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it; keep its default kind, as Carbon React does.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLFieldSetElement`.
Imports 
import { RadioButtonGroup } from 'carbon-components-ember/components';

  @readOnly={{false}}

>

ReasoningSteps

ai-chat-reasoning-steps · ./src/components/ai-chat/reasoning-steps.stories.gts
Displays a list of reasoning steps. Supports auto-open/close behavior or fully controlled state managed by the host. `ReasoningSteps` and its yielded `ReasoningStep` render a collapsible list of model-reasoning steps for [Carbon AI Chat](https://github.com/carbon-design-system/carbon-ai-chat) — the same disclosure shape as `ChainOfThought`, but without step numbering or status icons. A step without body content renders a static (non-interactive) header. Passing `@controlled={{true}}` to `ReasoningSteps` propagates `@controlled` to every yielded step: each step's own `@open` becomes the sole source of truth, and a click only calls `@onToggle`. The `Step*` stories mirror upstream's separate `Reasoning steps/Step` stories: `ReasoningStep` is only available as the component `ReasoningSteps` yields.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the panel that wraps this reasoning-steps list is open. |
| `@controlled` | `boolean` |  | When `true`, propagated to every yielded step as its own `@controlled`. |

## Blocks

- default block: Renders one `<ReasoningStep>` per step. Yields the step component pre-bound with `@controlled`, mirroring `Layer`'s `WithBoundArgs` pattern.
  - yields `ReasoningStep` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

ReasoningStepsToggle

ai-chat-reasoning-steps-toggle · ./src/components/ai-chat/reasoning-steps-toggle.stories.gts
A dedicated toggle button for expanding or collapsing reasoning steps. Compose it with `ReasoningSteps` when you want to manage the open state externally. The toggle is DOM-decoupled from the panel (same as `ChainOfThoughtToggle`/`ChainOfThought`): point `@panelId` at the `ReasoningSteps`' own `id` for `aria-controls`. With `@onToggle`, `@open` is controlled; without it, `@open` only seeds the initial state.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the panel this toggle controls is open. |
| `@openLabelText` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Hide reasoning steps'`. |
| `@closedLabelText` | `string` |  | Defaults to `'Show reasoning steps'`. |
| `@panelId` | `string` |  | `aria-controls` target — typically a `ReasoningSteps`' own id. |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@onToggle` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new open state whenever the button is clicked. |

Resizer

utilities-resizer · ./src/components/resizer.stories.gts
A draggable (and keyboard-operable) handle placed between two sibling elements. By default `Resizer` resizes its previous and next DOM siblings directly as it's dragged; pass `@onResize` to take full control instead (for example, to drive a CSS Grid's `grid-template-columns`). Any content passed to the default block is rendered inside the handle, which is useful for a custom drag icon. Drag the handle with a mouse, or focus it and use the arrow keys (hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> for larger steps, or press <kbd>Home</kbd>/<kbd>End</kbd> to jump to a boundary). Double-clicking the handle resets the siblings to the size they had when it was inserted. By design, the resting handle is a subtle `border-subtle`-colored 4px bar, much more visible on hover/focus (`border-interactive`). Carbon's docs suggest enhancing the trigger cue with a pseudo-element or custom children if needed; every story here widens the hit area with an invisible `::before`.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@orientation` (required) | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` |  | Whether the resizer handle is oriented horizontally (resize up/down) or vertically (resize left/right). |
| `@onResize` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, delta: number) => void` |  | Called on every resize movement with the delta (px) from the drag/key start position. When provided the component becomes fully controlled — sibling sizes are NOT updated automatically. |
| `@onResizeEnd` | `(event: MouseEvent \| KeyboardEvent, element: HTMLDivElement) => void` |  | Called once when a resize interaction ends (mouse-up, or a debounced moment after the last key-driven resize). Receives the resizer's element. |
| `@onDoubleClick` | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |  | Called on double-click. When provided, the default reset-to-initial- sizes behavior is suppressed. |
| `@thickness` | `number` |  | Thickness of the handle in px. Defaults to 4. |

## Blocks

- default block: Optional content rendered inside the handle (e.g. custom drag icons).

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLDivElement`.

Search

components-search · ./src/components/search.stories.gts
Search allows users to enter a term to be used to find specific content, filtering out results that don't match. `@onChange` is called with the `input` event on every change, as in Carbon React, so the term is `event.target.value`; debounce it yourself for an expensive search. Clearing the field with its close button or Escape calls it once more with the empty value, then calls `@onClear`. Pass `@defaultValue` for an uncontrolled field, or `@value` to set it.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@className` | `string` |  | Classes for the wrapper, as Carbon React's `className`. `class` and the other attributes go on the `<input>`. |
| `@onChange` | `(event: Event & { target: HTMLInputElement; }) => void` |  | Called with the `input` event on each change, as Carbon React's `onChange`, and once more when the field is cleared; the value is `event.target.value`. |
| `@onClear` | `() => void` |  | Called once the field is cleared, with its close button or Escape. |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@value` | `string` |  | The field's value. A new one replaces what was typed. |
| `@defaultValue` | `string` |  | The field's initial value, when it isn't controlled by `@value`. |
| `@placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xs"` |  |  |
| `@isLoading` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@expandable` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@light` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `@id` | `string` |  |  |
| `@closeButtonLabelText` | `string` |  |  |
| `@autoComplete` | `string` |  |  |
| `@type` | `string` |  |  |

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLInputElement`.

Select

components-select · ./src/components/select.stories.gts
`Select` is a native `<select>` styled as a Carbon field. Its options are the `SelectItem` it yields (`as |SelectItem|`), optionally grouped in `SelectItemGroup`s; the yielded one keeps `@value` selected as the options change. Attributes on the component, such as `name` or `required`, go to the `<select>`; `@className` styles the field's wrapper. Carbon recommends an empty option, selected by default: make the first `SelectItem` one with an empty `@value`. Without one, the first option is selected, or the one whose value is `@defaultValue`. Pass `@value` instead to control the selection: the select shows it, and goes back to it after a change that `@onChange` doesn't pass back.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@className` | `string` |  | Specify an optional className to be applied to the node containing the label and the select box. Attributes go to the `<select>`. |
| `@defaultValue` | `string \| number` |  | Optionally provide the default value of the `<select>` |
| `@disabled` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the control is disabled |
| `@helperText` | `string` |  | Provide text that is used alongside the control label for additional help |
| `@hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the label should be hidden, or not |
| `@id` | `string` |  | Specify a custom `id` for the `<select>` |
| `@inline` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether you want the inline version of this control |
| `@invalid` | `boolean` |  | Specify if the currently value is invalid. |
| `@invalidText` | `string` |  | Message which is displayed if the value is invalid. |
| `@labelText` | `string` |  | Provide label text to be read by screen readers when interacting with the control. |
| `@noLabel` | `boolean` |  | Reserved for use with Pagination component. Will not render a label for the select since Pagination renders one for us. |
| `@onChange` | `(event: Event & { target: HTMLSelectElement; }) => void` |  | Called with the `change` event on each change, as Carbon React's `onChange`; the value is `event.target.value`. |
| `@readOnly` | `boolean` |  | Whether the select should be read-only |
| `@size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xs"` |  | Specify the size of the Select Input. |
| `@value` | `string \| number` |  | The value of the `<select>`. While it's set, the select shows it, and goes back to it after a change `@onChange` doesn't pass back. |
| `@warn` | `boolean` |  | Specify whether the control is currently in warning state |
| `@warnText` | `string` |  | Provide the text that is displayed when the control is in warning state |

## Blocks

- default block: The options: the yielded `SelectItem`, optionally grouped in `SelectItemGroup`s. It keeps `@value` selected as the options change.
  - yields `SelectItem` (component)
- `<:decorator>`: **Experimental:** an AI label, or any other decorator, shown in the field. Yields an `AILabel` already set up for it.
  - yields `AILabel` (component)

## Element

`...attributes` are applied to `HTMLSelectElement`.

SessionShell

ai-chat-session-shell · ./src/components/ai-chat/session-shell.stories.gts
Info
No description found. Write a jsdoc comment such as /** Component description */.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@aiEnabled` | `boolean` |  | Enables AI-specific theming on the launcher and shell. |
| `@closedLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the closed launcher button. |
| `@messagesAriaLabel` | `string` |  | Aria label for the messages region. |
| `@instanceId` | `string` |  | Resolves which `ChatSession` this shell drives, via `@service('carbon.ai-chat-session').for(instanceId)` - for isolating several independent chat widgets on one page. Omit it for a single-widget page (resolves to the default session, matching this component's pre-multi-instance behavior). |
| `@historyItems` | `SessionShellHistoryItem[]` |  | Host-supplied list of past chat history items, rendered by `SessionShell`'s own default `<:history>` assembly (a `ChatHistory` built from `ChatHistoryHeader`/`Toolbar`/`Content`/`Panel`) - pass a `<:history>` block instead for full control. Host-owned rather than tracked by `carbon.ai-chat-session` itself, matching upstream's own division of responsibility (`HistoryService#loadHistory()`'s `customLoadHistory` host callback, not a Redux store slice) - see AGENTS.md. |
| `@selectedHistoryItemId` | `string` |  | Id of the currently-selected history item. |
| `@onHistoryItemSelect` | `(id: string) => void` |  |  |
| `@onHistoryItemRename` | `(id: string, name: string) => void` |  |  |
| `@onHistoryItemDelete` | `(id: string) => void` |  |  |

## Blocks

- `<:header>`: Shell header content, shown only while open.
- `<:history>`: History panel content. Overrides `SessionShell`'s own default `ChatHistory` assembly entirely when passed - see `@historyItems` and AGENTS.md's "Persistence and the `chat-history` integration" section for the session-owned/host-owned split the default assembly draws. This component only owns `@service('carbon.ai-chat-session').for(@instanceId).showHistory`/ `toggleHistory`, the same "inject the service, pass args down, don't prop-drill" boundary `ChatShell` itself already draws for every other slot - a filler that needs the same session this shell drives must resolve it with the same `@instanceId` this shell was given.
- `<:workspace>`: Workspace panel content. Left entirely to the caller - see `<:history>`.

## Element

SimpleBarChart

charts-simplebarchart · ./src/components/charts/simple-bar-chart.stories.gts
A simple bar chart, rendered by `@carbon/charts`. It yields `Axis` (one each for `left` and `bottom`, both required), `TabularData` (one per data group, from `@values` plus `@keys` or `@dates`, or from `@data`), `ColorScale` (a color per group) and `ColorPairing` (a Carbon color pairing). Load `@carbon/charts/styles.css` alongside the Carbon styles.
API description 
## Arguments

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@title` | `string` |  | The chart's title, rendered by |
| `@resizable` | `boolean` |  | Whether the chart resizes with its container. Defaults to `true`. |
| `@legendClickable` | `boolean` |  | Whether clicking a legend item shows or hides its data. Defaults to `true`. |

Slider

components-slider · ./src/components/slider.stories.gts
Sliders provide a visual indication of adjustable content, where the user can increase or decrease the value by moving the handle along a horizontal track. Slider is controlled: pass `@value` (and `@valueUpper` for a second handle) and update them from `@onChange`, which receives `{ value, valueUpper }`. The handles move with the pointer or the arrow keys (Shift multiplies the step by `@stepMultiplier`), and the text input(s) next to the track accept typed values.
